name: pixel-system-font
about: What the fidelity diff ignores on the Pixel shade, and why (D-038, D-041). tools/fidelity/maskgen.py reads stock's uiautomator trees (capture.sh --side stock --dump) and writes masks/pixel-system-font.json and masks/pixel-regions.json from these rules. A rule never hides a tile, the header or the first notification card, except the own bounds of a text node whose weight comes from a font-family name.

rules.why: A notification's title is set in the family-named style variable-title-small-emphasized (TextAppearance.DeviceDefault.Notification.Title): on a Pixel the family carries the semibold weight. The emulator has no such font and stock draws the title in plain Roboto, regular; ours draws Google Sans Flex at 600 (comp.qs.card.title). Weight and glyph widths cannot match here, so each title's own bounds (grown 40 px sideways for the wider bold text, 6 px up and down) are ignored, but the growth stops at the left edge of the row's time label and its divider (a 'now' that a wider title pushes aside stays a finding) and at the top edge of the body text below; the card's place, size, colour and the other text are still compared.
rules.evidence: docs/SHADE_PIXEL_EVALUATION.md lines 650-662 ('the emulator has no Google Sans ... a view style whose weight comes from a font family comes out regular'); app/src/main/assets/themes/pixel.json comp.qs.card.title (family google:Google Sans Flex, weight 600, src names variable-title-small-emphasized); stock's tree: TextView resource-id title in each notification row (fixture [231,646][996,697], Play Protect, Launcher safety); golden light/quick.png against ours: stock's 'Fidelity fixture' regular, ours semibold.

rules.why: The notification footer's Clear all button is set in variable-title-medium-emphasized (TextAppearance.NotificationFooterButton), a family-named style: stock draws it regular in Roboto, ours semibold in Google Sans Flex (comp.qs.clear.text). Only a 300 x 72 px box around the words (the node is the whole 640 px button) is ignored: the button's fill, shape and place stay in the comparison.
rules.evidence: docs/SHADE_PIXEL_EVALUATION.md lines 650 and 660; pixel.json comp.qs.clear.text (weight 600, src names variable-title-medium-emphasized); stock's tree: Button resource-id dismiss_text, text 'Clear all', bounds [220,1413][860,1539]; golden light/quick.png against ours: regular against semibold.

rules.why: OFF since the 2026-10-27 golden (B-062, D-041 addendum): both sides now list the '1 app is active' pill left of the footer's buttons (our own foreground service, Launcher safety), so the pill is compared. Stock's pill depends on the emulator's session: the 2026-10-26 golden had none (its tree's qs_footer_actions held the three buttons only, the first at x 672), and while that was so this rule ignored the row left of the user button (21 px less above and below, the pill's own height). Turn it on again for a golden whose stock footer has no pill.
rules.evidence: stock's tree (light/expanded.xml, 2026-10-27): qs_footer_actions [0,2179][1080,2337] holds a '1 app is active' row [42,2202][660,2328] before multi_user_switch [672,2201][798,2327], in every expanded state, light and dark; the golden's light/expanded.png shows it; ours' picture light/expanded.png: the pill at x 42-660, y 2210-2316.

rules.why: WEIGHED AND NOT USED: D-041 expected a stock-only Silent tail. The sides list the same rows (the fixture; Silent: Launcher safety; History / Clear all / Settings): the notification sets are equal (the manifest's notifications line, the fixed set since B-062: capture.sh snoozes other apps' notifications) and both pictures show the same rows, so nothing is ignored. Their differences (the cards' heights, the time label moved by a wider title) stay in the diff as findings.
rules.evidence: stock quick.xml (2026-10-27): the fixture's row at [42,546], the Silent row at [42,991] (Launcher safety), then the footer buttons at y 1218; golden manifest: 'pkg=dev.launcher.app id=1;pkg=dev.launcher.app id=1001;'. (The 2026-10-26 golden also listed Google Play Protect, on both sides then.)
